name: Brute Force: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries with no prior knowledge of legitimate credentials may guess passwords to attempt access to accounts, for example many failed SSH or web logins from one source against one account.
detection: Monitor many failed authentication attempts across a short window from a single source; alert when a failure burst is followed by a success.
mitigation: Account lockout (M1036), multi-factor authentication (M1032), password policies (M1027).

name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
description: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to attempt to acquire valid account credentials while avoiding lockouts.
detection: Monitor failed logins across many distinct usernames from the same source, including invalid user names.
mitigation: MFA (M1032), account lockout (M1036), disabling unused accounts.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to gain initial access, persistence, or privilege escalation. A successful login after a brute-force burst is a strong indicator.
detection: Correlate successful logins with prior failures, unusual source IPs, geographies or login times.
mitigation: MFA (M1032), privileged account management (M1026), user account management (M1018).

name: Remote Services: SSH
description: Adversaries may use valid accounts to log into remote machines using Secure Shell (SSH) and perform actions as the logged-on user.
detection: Monitor SSH logins from unexpected sources and root logins over SSH.
mitigation: Disable root login, key-based auth only, MFA, restrict SSH to bastion hosts.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system, such as SQL injection, path traversal, deserialization or JNDI injection in a web application.
detection: Inspect web logs and WAF events for injection payloads (UNION SELECT, ' OR 1=1, ../, ${jndi:), and abnormal 5xx responses.
mitigation: Patch management (M1051), WAF (M1050), application isolation (M1048), input validation.

name: Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
description: Adversaries may scan victims for vulnerabilities, often with automated tools such as sqlmap, nikto, nmap or nuclei, producing many 404s and recognizable user agents.
detection: Monitor for scanner user agents and high 4xx rates from one source.
mitigation: Pre-compromise; reduce exposed surface, rate limiting, WAF bot rules.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, e.g. by port scanning many destination ports from one source.
detection: Monitor firewall logs for one source hitting many distinct ports or hosts in a short window.
mitigation: Network segmentation (M1030), disable unnecessary services (M1042), IDS/IPS (M1031).

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution, for example via command injection into subprocess calls with shell=True, or downloading and piping scripts to sh.
detection: Monitor process execution of sh/bash spawned by web servers; look for curl|sh or wget patterns.
mitigation: Avoid shell invocation with untrusted input, execution prevention (M1038).

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
description: Adversaries may perform sudo caching and/or use the sudoers file to elevate privileges, or exploit sudo vulnerabilities such as CVE-2021-3156.
detection: Monitor sudo usage by unexpected users, especially shortly after a suspicious login.
mitigation: Restrict sudoers, patch sudo, privileged account management (M1026).

name: Create Account: Local Account
description: Adversaries may create a local account to maintain access to victim systems, e.g. via useradd after compromise.
detection: Monitor useradd/adduser events and new entries in /etc/passwd.
mitigation: MFA, privileged account management, alert on account creation.

name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
description: Adversaries may backdoor web servers with web shells, such as uploaded .php or .jsp files that accept commands.
detection: Monitor web logs for requests to newly created script files with cmd= parameters.
mitigation: Restrict file uploads, file integrity monitoring.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories, including attempts to read /etc/passwd via path traversal in web parameters.
detection: Look for ../ sequences and sensitive file names in request URIs.
mitigation: Input validation, least privilege for service accounts.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a different protocol than the existing command and control channel, such as large outbound transfers on unusual ports.
detection: Monitor for large outbound transfers to rare destinations or non-standard ports.

name: Network Denial of Service
description: Adversaries may perform network denial of service to degrade or block availability, e.g. HTTP floods or HTTP/2 rapid reset.
detection: Monitor request rates and connection resets per source.
mitigation: Rate limiting, DDoS protection, filter network traffic (M1037).

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment, e.g. curl or wget fetching a script from an attacker-controlled server.
detection: Monitor for curl/wget to rare external hosts, especially run as root or piped to a shell.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols to avoid detection by blending in with existing traffic.
detection: Analyze network data for uncommon data flows and processes that normally do not make network connections.
mitigation: Network intrusion prevention (M1031), filter network traffic (M1037).

name: Non-Standard Port
description: Adversaries may communicate using a protocol and port pairing that are typically not associated, such as a reverse shell on TCP 4444 (Metasploit default).
detection: Alert on outbound connections to ports such as 4444, 1337, 31337 from servers.
